**Split the PAR 1× vs 5× dose-response by cell line** (separate DE runs, or `~ cell_line * condition`) — the pooled contrast cannot test the cross-line arm asymmetry the ChIP suggests

**Sequencing forensics (7/21):** demux stats show all 12 ChIP libraries got 10.8–26M reads; the four low-yield SKOV3 Tier-2 IPs failed on **library complexity**, not depth. Re-sequencing recovers nothing → **re-ChIP is the remedy.** Pooling and run quality were both fine.

**Resolve the peak-count discrepancy vs Goetsch** (his counts are higher at `-npeak=40000` vs Karl's 300000). Two live candidates, both about method differences rather than a defect: (a) **ask Goetsch whether he deduplicates and blacklists** — Karl runs the full ENCODE cascade (`markdup -r`, `-f 2 -q 30 -F 1804`, blacklist) and retained 37%; skipping dedup on ~67%-duplicate libraries would give ~3× the reads into peak calling; (b) check whether PE BAMs went into SPP without tagAlign/R1 conversion — **SPP is a single-end tool** and estimates fragment length by strand cross-correlation

~~ALT-contig hypothesis~~ — **excluded 7/21.** Index was built from `GRCh38.primary_assembly.genome.fa`, which carries no ALT contigs or patches. Re-aligning to `no_alt_analysis_set` would change nothing.

Truncating regionPeaks to 40k as a test — **rejected** (Karl): IDR is designed to consume a relaxed peak list and needs the noise tail to fit its irreproducible component; truncating adds stringency mid-pipeline and lowers the ceiling

**Test the E2F4/E2F5 hypothesis from existing data** — pull `E2F4`, `E2F5`, `E2F1`, `E2F2`, `RBL1` normalized counts from the DESeq2 object; E2F5 ≫ E2F4 would convert the gap into a specific antibody order
**Test E2F4 antibody cross-reactivity** — `bedtools jaccard` HEYA8 E2F4 pre-IDR peaks vs HEYA8 E2F1 peaks
Motif analysis underneath the carrier peaks — E2F sites (`TTTSSCGC`/`GCGSSAAA`) under E2F1/Rb; CHR (`TTYGAA`) under LIN54/p130/E2F4. HOMER or MEME-ChIP/CentriMo
Cross-factor overlap (`bedtools intersect`/`jaccard`, UpSet) — test the predicted LIN54/E2F4/p130 and E2F1/Rb groupings, and the partial-but-imperfect overlap between them
deepTools promoter heatmap: proliferating RNA-seq then treated RNA-seq, ordered by ChIP signal
Set up IGV for track-level peak inspection
Load samtools on HRI → exact read counts + duplicate rates to replace the BAM-size estimates
Confirm what the final-filter step drops on the low-complexity libraries (MAPQ vs proper-pair vs blacklist) — retention was 9–12% vs 37% on the good pair
**Order/validate a new E2F4 antibody** — E2F4 produced nothing usable in either cell line across 4 libraries at good depth, and it is the subunit that defines DREAM. Consider adding E2F5 and p107.

**Inventoried what's on HRI (7/21).** RNA is **complete** — all 42 libraries present and trimmed in `PAR/RNA/fastp` (18 core DE + 6 reversibility + 9 FT282 + 9 prolif). ChIP runs 018 + 019 all present. **Only `PG015S–X` are missing** — the six run-15 ChIP pilots.

Confirm all 42 RNA libraries have STAR count tables (`ls PAR/RNA/star/*ReadsPerGene* | wc -l`) — fastqs present ≠ counts generated
**Agree comparison criteria with Goetsch before parallel ChIP runs** — genome build, blacklist, input pooling scheme, IDR threshold. He has not run SPP or IDR yet.
Intersect the carrier IDR peaks (HEYA8 E2F1, SKOV3 p130, HEYA8 LIN54) with the DESeq2 DE results — ChIPseeker annotate to nearest TSS, then test against the dose-response gene sets
Build the QC-discriminator table (per IP: reads · NSC · RSC · quality tag · NRF/PBC · median fragment size · IDR peaks) — separates technical failure from biological absence before any claim
Reinvestigate reps that looked healthy but collapsed at IDR — esp. HEYA8_E2F4 (53,661 peaks in one rep, 0 surviving) and SKOV3_LIN54
Stage 05: deepTools supervised signal at motif-anchored promoters (Rb+E2F1 at E2F sites; p130+E2F4+LIN54 at CHR/CDE) → annotate peaks → intersect RNA-seq DE
Fix the cosmetic `04a` echo label ("single-replicate tier" copied from 04b)
Acquire the 6 remaining run-15 ChIP fastqs (`PG015S–X`)
~~Generate counts for the remaining RNA samples~~ — **already complete: 42/42 `ReadsPerGene` present; job 38670 COMPLETED all tasks.** RNA is done through counts.

Visualize the exoRNA characterization results — `04_plot_composition.R` + a new `theme_exo.R` built; figures in `R_Projects/exorna/figures/`. **BUT the composition figure is premature — see the pipeline issues below. Don't send it yet.**

**⚠ THE LOAD-BEARING FIX: the classify cascade runs PE-concordant on small-RNA inserts.** `03_classify_smallrna.sbatch` DECISION 1 (line ~59): inserts (~20–35 nt) are shorter than the 101 nt reads, so concordant PE alignment fails and dumps real small RNA into `--un-conc` → unassigned. This likely **deflates tRNA/miRNA AND inflates unassigned at the same time.** Fix = merge mates first (`fastp --merge`), run the cascade single-end, diff the composition. Do this before trusting any of the tRNA/miRNA/unassigned numbers.

rRNA numbers **already exist** — `code/exorna/figures/fig_rRNA_burden.R` has them from the 7/19 SortMeRNA logs: MDA231 95.0/89.5/80.0%, MCF10a 12.1/7.2/6.3%. No pull needed; feed these into the two-tier Fig 1 (Panel A = rRNA split, Panel B = non-rRNA breakdown).

tRNA near-zero is **partly reference too**: index is genomic GtRNAdb (missing 3′ CCA) + end-to-end-ish alignment. Test whether tRNA is hiding in the `genome` bin (intersect the kept genome BAM with tRNA loci) — the QC block at the bottom of the classify script already logged "rRNA reads also mapping tRNA", so check those logs first.

miRNA may be **inflated**: index is miRBase `hsa_hairpin` (precursor, ~85 nt), not mature, with `--local -L 18` → permissive. Verify via read-length distribution of miRNA-assigned reads (real mature = ~22 nt) and whether they concentrate on MDA231-expressed miRNAs.

**Nothing in the exoRNA pipeline is deduped.** For small-RNA bins that's arguably correct (no UMIs; identical real molecules). For the mito/gDNA finding, measure duplication (`samtools markdup -s` on the genome BAM, as a readout not a removal) to pressure-test it.

**⚠ MDA231_rep1 chrM = a finding, not an artifact to discard** (Karl's reframe): MDA231 EVs are mito-enriched *consistently* (reps 2/3 at 2–4% = 15–30× MCF10a's 0.1%; rep1 at 47% = ~300×). Real EV-mtDNA biology (breast-cancer EV mtDNA transfer lit, e.g. Sansone PNAS ~2017 — verify). Show all three reps; the cargo-vs-co-purified question needs a DNase protection assay (future work), not exclusion.

**⚠ Duplicate `theme_exo.R` — reconcile before committing.** Two files, incompatible token names: `code/exorna/theme_exo.R` (new, `EXO_CLASS_COLORS`/`EXO_LINE_COLORS`) and `code/exorna/figures/theme_exo.R` (7/19, `pal_class`/`pal_cellline`/`ink_*`). `fig_rRNA_burden.R` sources the latter. Merge to one canonical theme.
Send Bianca the composition table + figure only after the PE-merge rerun; the rRNA split (Panel A) is solid now and could go earlier if she needs something.

projects.name: The CT gene paper
projects.status: Newly logged (7/20). Two MS theses (Clara, Zayne) are the foundation; 28-gene shortlist in hand. Karl's contribution is lit review + terminology/ontology + discussion.
projects.identity: how cancer/testis (CT) genes get **activated in the first place**: a coordinated germ-cell program, or stochastic noise? The field has largely studied CT *antigens* as immunotherapy targets and treats activation as stochastic; this asks the mechanistic question underneath. Built on two lab MS theses — **Clara Mosentine** (50 CT genes elevated in stage IV; most known CT genes activate *early*, not at metastasis) and **Zayne** (TCGA/GTEx/cell-line differential expression → a 28-gene mechanistic shortlist). Proposed discriminating test: compare testis-vs-normal, cancer-vs-normal, then (testis/normal) vs (cancer/normal); open threads include separating cancer-germline from cancer-testis, and comparison against embryo data. **Karl's contribution is conceptual and written, not computational** — literature review; the semantics, etymology, and ontology of this niche's terminology; and the discussion (what "germline" means, and whether a soma-to-germline program in tumorigenesis is credible or stochastic).
